title: Inverse-image ideal annihilation under closed pushforward
statement: Let $j:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion], $L$ a quasi-coherent ideal on $Z$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], and $t\in\mathbb N$. Let $F$ be a quasi-coherent module on $Z$ and $H$ a quasi-coherent module on $X$ [pqf-def-coherent], with an isomorphism $e:H\cong j_*F$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. If the ideal-power product $L^tF$ is zero [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-module-product-stalk], then $((L^t).\operatorname{map}(j))H$ is zero. Here map is the ideal of the composite closed immersion $(L^t).\mathrm{subscheme}\to Z\to X$. No Noetherianity or formal-system assumption is required.

source.place: Theorem 088E (theorem-grothendieck-existence), closed quotient replacement; affine product calculation of Tags 01Y9 and 01I8. Proof assembled from the cited affine-section results, verified at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/088E.

proof.text: Use the cover by all affine opens of Z and the ideal-power zero criterion to obtain that L(V)^t annihilates F(V) for every affine V.

For affine U in X its inverse image V is affine. Mathlib IdealSheafData.ideal_map_of_isAffineHom and ideal_pow identify the mapped ideal on U with the inverse image of L(V)^t. Pushforward restricts scalars, and the sectionwise linear equivalence induced by e transfers annihilation to H(U).

The affine product-section formula puts the range of the product inclusion in the submodule generated by these zero products. Its injective inclusion implies zero sections on every affine open. Affine opens form a basis, so sheaf separatedness gives the zero sheaf (WeilConjectures Modules.isZero_of_forall_affineOpens).
